chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that were established by the Light
chapter_note: Aside from a short formulaic opening frame, the chapter is a tightly structured, impersonal triadic exposition of eschatological cosmology: three necessary constructions by the Light (new earth; coffin/prison for the Enemy; fate of the condemned) culminating in the mechanics of eternal separation/sterilisation. Despite one paragraph using moral vocabulary (“sinners”, “wicked deeds”), it functions as doctrinal mechanism within the cosmic system rather than institutional exhortation.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic/dialogue opener (“Once again he speaks to his disciples…”), functioning as editorial container rather than teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Three things would be fashioned by the Light through necessity. For there can be no other way nor other result, to allow them to stay without coming about. For the Darkness, the Enemy, must be bound by them; he who stood up against the Light from the beginning. Due to this, these things have no (other) result, to allow them to stay without coming about.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, necessity-driven cosmological exposition; establishes a numbered structure (“Three things…”) with no audience-address, citation, or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the first thing is the new luminous earth, which was set and built on top of this earth [ ... ] it, namely that alien body [ ... ] built upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered triad with cosmic-architectural content (new earth built over this earth); register remains within cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: The second thing is this: They will [ ... ] and they [ ... ] the new earth, the coffin [ ... ] ⟨p.105⟩ of the Dark Fire, the companion of the Enemy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic continuation of the triad; “coffin…prison” language remains part of the eschatological cosmic mechanism (containment of Dark Fire/Enemy).

paragraphs.core_text: The third thing is the souls of all the sinners who have been condemned by their deeds. They were [ ... ] over them woe; they have been condemned according to the wicked deeds they had committed, and due to this they will be crucified on the Enemy, he who had raised himself up against the Greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Moral vocabulary is present, but the paragraph still serves the triadic cosmological schema: it specifies the third necessary result and its eschatological placement (“crucified on the Enemy”), without institutional rules or second-person exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: They will seal up this final lump when all the likenesses and images of every shape will be nailed in it. Also, those will be bound by this last fetter for eternity, and be placed as a footstool and a mat and a rag for this coffin [ ... ] which is the prison of the Enemy. It will be placed, being a boundary-marker and a great void between the two, between the Darkness and the Enemy, so that they cannot reach one another, nor can they hear their voices; rather they will become sterile as they are separated from each other for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly mechanistic cosmic closure: sealing, binding, boundary-marker/void, and sterilising separation of Darkness and Enemy—hallmarks of systematic eschatological cosmology rather than later application.
